result.summary: The Illinois Municipal Retirement Fund (IMRF) seeks proposals for bundled or separate general investment consulting, real estate consulting, and performance measurement services for its Board of Trustees and Investment Department Staff. IMRF will not reimburse proposal preparation expenses and may reject any or all proposals. Staff will evaluate submissions; firms may be invited to present to the Investment Committee and/or Board, and consultant selection requires Board approval. The goal is an ongoing relationship providing advice and technical support for managing IMRF’s diversified, multibillion-dollar investment portfolio using current analytical techniques, concepts, and professional services.

result.summary: The Quiet Period runs from issuance of the investment consultant RFP until the Board selects a consultant or declares the process complete. Respondents must not contact IMRF Board members about the search and should direct questions to the designated investment or executive contacts listed in the RFP. Incumbent consultant respondents may communicate with Board members but may not discuss the search. The period promotes equal access to information, consistent and accurate communications, and an efficient, diligent, and fair process; it will be posted on the IMRF website to help prevent violations. Board members and staff not directly involved in the search must not discuss related products or services with respondents, except during formal search site visits or interviews. Violating the Quiet Period disqualifies a respondent, and offering or providing anything of value to Board members or staff is inappropriate.

result.summary: IMRF’s portfolio is globally diversified, with a market value shown as a placeholder date and amount. About 99% is managed primarily with full discretion by external investment managers; roughly 1% is managed internally in cash equivalents. The Northern Trust Company is master trustee. Target and current allocations are listed as placeholders across U.S. fixed income, domestic and international equities, real estate, alternatives, and cash. Long-term objectives are to exceed the 7.5% actuarial return assumption with minimal risk, diversify risky assets, and beat inflation by an estimated 5.5% over a market cycle. Additional moving-period targets are specified: domestic equities should beat the Dow Jones U.S. Total Stock Market Total Return Index and inflation by at least 6% over five years; fixed income should beat the Barclays Aggregate Bond Index and inflation by 3% over five years; international equities should beat the MSCI ACWI ex-U.S.; real estate should exceed the NCREIF NPI by 1% before fees over three years; and alternatives should return over 12% over five years.

result.summary: The consultant will advise on investment goals, policies, asset allocation and risk/return modeling, and assist with rebalancing and transitions. It will review manager guidelines, benchmarks, contracts and fees, recommend changes, and participate in negotiations. Ongoing monitoring will assess portfolio and manager performance, strategy execution, benchmarks, stability and contract compliance; identify underperformance; and recommend and help implement corrective action. The consultant will calculate performance, reconcile return discrepancies, and provide monthly and quarterly written and verbal reports to the Board. Manager searches will use maintained databases, including minority-, women- and disability-owned firms, with nondiscriminatory practices. The consultant will prepare and support approved searches and public RFPs, assess responses, conduct due diligence and interviews, report results, explain exclusions of diverse firms, and assist the Committee and Board in selecting managers. Other duties include identifying investment opportunities or restructuring needs and educating Trustees and Staff. Attendance includes specified Board, committee, roundtable, manager and due-diligence meetings (estimated 60 meeting days annually), plus frequent calls and other reasonable pension-plan consulting services.

result.title: PART 5-- Specifications for the Assignment
result.summary: The section sets out the final contract framework: IMRF and the selected firm(s) will agree on detailed services and performance expectations; the contract supersedes the RFP, incorporates the RFP and proposal, and requires written acknowledgment of fiduciary status. General advisory includes meeting attendance and research, annual asset-allocation, capital-market, manager-allocation and investment-policy reviews, rebalancing support, up to five qualifying manager searches, roundtable support, access to research and education, and ongoing staff and trustee assistance. Separate project work may include asset-liability modeling and a review of the Alternatives Portfolio’s composition, benefits, capacity, potential investments, benchmarks and policy. Real estate advisory covers meetings, annual policy and portfolio reviews, pacing, investment sourcing and due diligence, ongoing manager monitoring, recommendations, four quarterly performance reports, research and availability. Performance services include monthly and quarterly customized reporting, separate Private Equity reports, Principal attendance at meetings, ongoing manager due diligence and communication of significant developments and recommended assignment changes.

Monthly reports cover total-fund and manager performance, index returns, key events, and asset allocation, excluding separate Real Estate and Private Equity reporting. Quarterly reports cover total-fund, asset-class, and manager performance; market conditions and events; indexes; asset allocation; return attribution; and written portfolio commentary on objectives, benchmarks, performance factors, and manager organizational issues. result.summary: Firms must answer every question in RFP Paragraphs 1.2–1.4, in order, with clearly linked supporting information; promotional or extraneous material may lead to rejection. They must estimate IMRF staff time (Appendix A) and provide firm and contact details. The questionnaire covers organizational structure, fiduciary status, history, ownership, services, finances, legal and regulatory matters, continuity, conflicts, capacity, databases, client and public-pension experience, and Illinois business-enterprise eligibility. It requests staff qualifications, responsibilities, workload, availability, retention, training, diversity, and backup coverage. Investment and real estate consulting responses address philosophy, allocation, risk and return, asset classes, manager searches, fees, performance monitoring, benchmarks, manager changes, client usage of IMRF-listed managers, and communications. Performance-measurement responses cover data validation, reconciliation, reporting, attribution, benchmarks, GIPS, and real estate and alternatives. Firms must identify account personnel, disclose revenue from performance measurement, and propose retainer, bundled, and special-service fees with billing methods and all costs. Required appendices include organizational, compliance, continuity, conflict, database, biography, and public-fund materials.

nodes.title: 10.3 ORGANIZATION, STAFF QUALIFICATIONS AND RELEVANT EXPERIENCE
nodes.summary: The section presents an RFP questionnaire for investment, real estate, and performance-measurement firms covering organizational structure, fiduciary status, history, ownership and affiliates, services, offices, revenues, finances, regulatory and legal matters, business continuity, growth and transaction plans, capacity, conflicts, investment-manager databases and inclusion criteria, and Illinois business-enterprise eligibility. It requests five-year totals for assets advised and clients; current U.S. tax-exempt pension-account details, including public funds; terminated institutional relationships and former-client contacts; and public-pension references. Personnel questions cover staffing, roles, locations, qualifications, experience, education, tenure, account responsibilities, consultant biographies and backup coverage, client and asset loads, public-pension experience, departures, compensation, retention, training, availability, and workforce diversity. Consulting topics include investment philosophy, objectives, allocation methods and target ranges, risk/return assumptions, non-U.S. and alternative assets, indexing, currency hedging, manager-search resources and criteria, a recent search example, and three-year search activity across equity and fixed-income markets.

nodes.title: A. ORGANIZATIONAL SUMMARY
nodes.summary: An RFP questionnaire for investment consulting, real estate consulting, and performance measurement services requests firm/contact details and information on organizational structure, staff qualifications, and experience. It asks firms to identify fiduciary classifications; describe their history, ownership, affiliates, joint ventures, consulting capabilities, organization chart, offices, account-service locations, business lines, and revenue sources. Applicants must provide financial-condition information, ADV Part II, and business-continuity/disaster-recovery policies, and discuss growth plans, client and consultant capacity, resource expansion, mergers, acquisitions, and spin-offs. The questionnaire also covers legal proceedings, broker/dealer status and trading, investment-management services and clients, staff board service and compensation, and conflicts-of-interest policies and enforcement. It requests the size and listings of investment-manager databases, including separate databases and inclusion criteria for minority-, women-, and disability-owned firms, plus disclosure of relevant clients and revenues. Finally, it asks whether the firm qualifies under Illinois’s business-enterprise definitions for these ownership groups.

nodes.title: B. ASSETS ADVISED
nodes.summary: Requests asset-adviser information: total assets advised and number of clients across all asset classes for five year-end dates; a list of current U.S. tax-exempt pension accounts showing client name (or fund type if confidential), inception date, market value, and portfolio description, with public pension funds highlighted; details of U.S. tax-exempt institutional client relationships terminated in the past three years, including number, names, asset values, reasons, and contact details for three former clients; and contact information for three U.S. tax-exempt public pension fund consulting clients as references.

nodes.title: C. PERSONNEL
nodes.summary: Requests staffing totals and a roster of principal officers, consultants, and client-service staff, including locations, roles, duties, experience, education, firm tenure, and IMRF-account responsibility. Requires biographies and coverage arrangements for primary and backup consultants; primary consultant assets advised, clients, other duties, and public-pension experience; senior departures and replacements, compensation and incentives, retention programs, staff training, and meeting availability. Also requests a firm-wide full-time workforce diversity profile by work group and demographic category, with rules for classifying minority women; the 2008 sample table reports zero employees in all listed roles and categories. Related consulting questions cover investment philosophy, goals, asset-allocation methods and responsibilities, target ranges and changes, risk/return assumptions and their evolution, non-U.S. assets, alternatives, indexing, currency hedging, manager-search resources and criteria, a recent search example and outcome, and searches supported over three years across U.S. and global equity and fixed income, and international equity and fixed income.

nodes.title: C. PERSONNEL (intro)
nodes.summary: The personnel section requests staffing totals by role, and a roster of principal officers, consultants, and client-service officers with names, locations, titles, responsibilities, experience, education, and firm tenure, identifying those responsible for the IMRF account. It requires detailed biographies and tenure for the primary and backup consultants; the primary consultant’s assets advised, client count, and other duties; and public-pension experience, including first-client year and current public-fund assets and client numbers. It asks about backup coverage, senior staff departures over three years and replacements, compensation and incentive bonuses, staff-retention programs, consultant/research/performance staff training, and the primary consultant’s availability for client and investment-manager meetings. It also requests a firm-wide diversity profile of full-time employees by work group and demographic category, using the most current data, with stated rules for classifying minority women.

It requests current target allocation ranges and how and why they have changed; recommended portfolio risk and return assumptions, including differences by investment horizon or public versus private assets and changes over time; guidance on non-U.S.-dollar assets, alternatives, indexation, and currency hedging for U.S. tax-exempt clients; and manager-search capabilities, database development and maintenance, and recommendation criteria. nodes.summary: The RFP asks firms to identify account personnel, explain backup arrangements, and provide biographies; disclose the share of revenue from performance measurement; and submit separate annual-retainer fee proposals for general investment, real estate investment, and performance measurement consulting, plus optional bundled fees. Proposals must include fees for special services outside retainers and cover all administrative, third-party, travel, and service costs. Firms must explain fee calculation and billing. Required appendices cover IMRF requirements; organizational charts; ADV Part II or comparable report; business continuity and disaster recovery; conflicts and enforcement; investment-manager database and listings of minority-, women-, or disability-owned businesses in it; primary and backup consultant biographies; and public-fund experience.
